newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's 1330 GMT release of the U.S. October personal income and consumption data, dealers said on Friday.
Personal income for October is forecast to be unchanged from a 0.6 percent increase reported in September.
October personal consumption is expected to show an increase of 0.3 percent against a 0.1 percent gain reported in September.
"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments," a local dealer said.
"The market is now waiting for tonight's (U.S. October) personal income and consumption figures for more clues to market direction," he said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact here as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend," he added.
In day-to-day rates, weekend rose 3/8 percentage point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent, Monday/Tuesday was unchanged from Thursday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 and week-fixed rose 1/16 point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-1/2 5-3/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent.
